description: Lesson content on verifying that a given function solves a differential equation, the antiderivative link (y' = f(x) implies y = the integral of f(x) dx), and the distinction between the general solution (with an arbitrary constant) and a particular solution (constant fixed by an initial condition y(x0) = y0).

lessons.title: When a function is a solution of a differential equation
lessons.statement_latex: y = f(x) \text{ is a solution of a differential equation if substituting it (and its derivatives) into the equation satisfies it identically.}

lessons.title: Verify y = cos x solves y'' + y = 0
lessons.statement_latex: \text{Show that } y = \cos x \text{ is a solution of } y'' + y = 0.
solution_steps: y = \cos x \implies y' = -\sin x \implies y'' = -\cos x
lessons.answer_latex: \text{Yes: } y = \cos x \text{ is a solution of } y'' + y = 0.

lessons.title: y' = f(x) implies y = the antiderivative of f(x), worked on y' = 2x^2
lessons.statement_latex: \frac{dy}{dx} = f(x) \iff dy = f(x)\,dx \iff \int dy = \int f(x)\,dx \iff y = \int f(x)\,dx + c

lessons.title: Fixing the constant with an initial condition (particular solution)
